title: SDLC configuration (agent-setup)
description: The single machine-readable description of a repository's SDLC. Hooks, skills and agents read this file instead of hardcoding branch names and gate commands, which is what makes them portable. Lives at .agents/sdlc.config.json (a legacy .ai/sdlc.config.json is still read). Keys starting with an underscore are comments or markers (_comment, _provisional) and are ignored by the tooling.

^_.description: Comment or marker, e.g. _comment. Ignored by hooks and skills.

version.description: Config format version. Bump only on a breaking change to this schema.

kind.description: Free text: 'monorepo', 'library', 'service', 'mobile app', 'CLI'. Used only in generated prose.

stack.description: e.g. ["TypeScript", "Node 23", "pnpm", "Next.js"]. The installer and /sdlc-init detect these; correct them by hand if they guess wrong.

runtime.description: Minimum runtime that actually works, not what the manifest claims. e.g. "node>=23.6".

branching.description: Which branch is production, where work lands, and whether an agent may move production on its own.

model.description: two-trunk: production + integration (main/develop). trunk: one branch, short-lived feature branches. gitflow: adds release/* and hotfix/* lines.

production.description: The branch that is deployed. Never written by an agent unless releaseOnRequestOnly is false.

integration.description: Where day-to-day work lands and where feature branches are cut from. Omit for the trunk model; production is then also the integration branch.

featurePrefix.description: Proposed prefix when the session hook suggests a branch name.

hotfixPrefix.description: gitflow only: branches with this prefix may be cut from production (and merge into both lines).

releaseOnRequestOnly.description: true = an agent never pushes, merges or opens a PR to a separate production branch on its own initiative (on a trunk, pull requests into it are the normal path). guard-git.mjs enforces it in Claude Code sessions; branch protection on the git host enforces it for everyone. false switches the production-write denials off.

protectedRefs.description: Extra refs treated as production for guard purposes, e.g. ["release/*", "staging"]. Globs allowed.

sharedTree.description: true when more than one agent session works in this checkout at once. Enables the broad-staging denials (git add -A / . / -u, git commit -a, git stash without paths) and the 're-check status before committing' instruction.

scopes.description: Allowed commit scopes. Empty means unconstrained.

trailers.description: Lines appended to every commit message, e.g. a Co-Authored-By trailer.

gates.description: Every check that must pass before work merges, cheapest first. /gates (run-gates.mjs) runs this list in order; the gate-runner agent runs it in its own context.

id.description: Stable slug. Referenced by critical-infrastructure.md and by CI job names.

command.description: Exactly what CI runs. If it differs from CI, this file is lying.

blocking.description: false = reported but does not block a merge. Be honest here; an advisory gate marked blocking is how a green build starts meaning nothing.

rule.description: The rule id from rules.md that this gate holds up. Omit if the gate enforces no stated rule.

expectNonZero.description: true for a command that exits non-zero by design and whose real verdict comes from a comparison step. Prevents a runner reporting a designed exit code as a failure.

when.description: Glob patterns. The gate runs only if the working diff touches a matching path. Omit to always run.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the gate after this long (default 15 minutes) and report it as failed — an inconclusive gate fails closed.

fix.description: The first thing to try when this gate fails. Shown verbatim in the /gates failure report.

root.description: Where the knowledge base lives (.agents by default; .ai for a separate tool-agnostic tree).

rules.description: Path to the numbered invariant register. Point it at the existing document (and section) if the rules already live elsewhere.

plan.description: The living work-schedule document, if the repo has one. Read by the handoff skill.

guard.description: What the guards deny. Every denial names its correct alternative, so an agent retries without needing the user.

denyBroadStaging.description: Defaults to the value of sharedTree.

denyCommitOnProduction.description: two-trunk/gitflow: deny commits while standing on a protected branch.

denyForcePushShared.description: Deny force-pushing or deleting the integration branch.

denyDiscardUncommitted.description: Deny reset --hard, checkout/restore of the whole tree, and clean -f when they would destroy uncommitted or untracked work.

denyNoVerify.description: Deny --no-verify on commit and push, and setting the git-hook escape variable — hooks exist to catch problems; the fix is the cause, not the hook.

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression source, matched against the shell command with heredoc and here-string bodies stripped.

instead.description: The command the agent should run instead.

postEdit.description: Fast checks surfaced immediately after an Edit/Write to a matching path. Keep this list short and the commands under a second — a hook that comments on every write becomes noise an agent learns to skim, which is worse than no hook.

paths.description: Glob patterns (**, *, ?, {a,b}) matched against the repo-relative edited path.

run.description: Command to execute. Its output is shown only on failure.

remind.description: Static text shown when a path matches. Use when there is no cheap command.

workflow.description: The kit's workflow hooks. Change a default only with a reason.

sessionSummary.description: session-eval shows the person one line of eval metrics and one of cost at session start (a systemMessage: the model never sees it). Off by default: the numbers are the admin's, read with agent-setup evals, usage and report.

verifyBeforeStop.description: stop-check blocks the end of a turn once when code changed after the last passing check.

contextWarnTokens.description: context-budget notes the agent when a window passes this many tokens, and again at each further multiple. 0 turns it off.

promptIntake.description: prompt-intake asks the agent to restate a large or risky task prompt (auth, payments, data, production, secrets) as a brief (goal, scope, acceptance, assumptions, risks) before its first edit.

promptCoach.description: Retired in 3.0: prompt-intake no longer coaches the developer. Has no effect; delete it.

retroEvery.description: agent-setup report lists a retro as due after this many recorded context windows without one. 0 turns it off.

askBranch.description: branch-check tells the agent to ask the user which branch to work on before its first edit. Off by default: the agent decides (small work on the integration branch, larger work on a new feature branch) and names the branch in its brief.

models.description: This project's changes to the kit's model tiers and prices (.agents/models.json — never edit the copy). `agent-setup update` writes the tiers into the agent files of tools that read their own format (Codex); the usage report prices sessions with the prices. For Claude Code, point an alias at another model with the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL settings instead.

prices.description: Per model id: this project's own rates (a negotiated discount, a cloud provider's price), or a model the kit does not list. USD per million tokens; the fields merge over the kit's card.

tiers.description: Per provider (anthropic, openai, google, or a new one) and tier: the model, or { model, effort }, to run that tier on instead of the kit's.

reference.description: What the usage report compares the actual cost with: main (each window's main model), a tier (frontier, high, medium, low) or a model id.

alias.description: Claude Code's alias for it (fable, opus, sonnet, haiku).

effort.description: The reasoning effort the tier runs at.
